question: Should broad sweep and commit-review capacity globally yield to a healthy target-admissible exact-review backlog using the proposed 16-worker congested and 4-worker saturated caps?
rationale: The patch can implement either policy correctly, but tests cannot decide the desired tradeoff between exact-item latency and broad maintenance throughput.

options.title: Approve after runtime proof
options.body: Accept the adaptive-priority policy after redacted Actions evidence demonstrates saturation throttling, stale or malformed telemetry fail-open behavior, bounded continuation requeue, and automatic recovery.

options.title: Approve monitored rollout
options.body: Record a proof override, merge with the proposed caps, and require immediate post-deployment observation with a rollback or tuning plan if broad maintenance starves.

options.title: Keep independent allowances
options.body: Decline global cross-lane throttling and retain separate broad defaults until a different admission policy is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve after runtime proof
recommendation.body: Accept the adaptive-priority policy after redacted Actions evidence demonstrates saturation throttling, stale or malformed telemetry fail-open behavior, bounded continuation requeue, and automatic recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their immediately preceding merged work owns exact-review capacity and backlog recovery, so they are best positioned to decide the intended throughput balance.
